That is the opposite of the contract this change states (unknown, never reported as changed) and of `test_an_unreadable_file_is_unknown_not_gone`, which only patches `read_bytes` after a successful `is_file()`. chunk_findings.detail: `file_digest` treats “unreadable” as absent whenever `Path.is_file()` fails. CPython’s `is_file()` swallows `OSError` from `stat` and returns False, so the `read_bytes` branch never runs and the new `OSError` handler in `_current` never sees the error. Given a recorded plugin (or other `FILE_KINDS` artifact) whose parent directory is mode `0o000`, `is_file()` is False, `file_digest` returns None, and `read` appends `{**artifact, "now": None}` — gone — even though the file was not removed. That is the opposite of the contract this change states (unknown, never reported as changed) and of `test_an_unreadable_file_is_unknown_not_gone`, which only patches `read_bytes` after a successful `is_file()`. Offboarding that trusts `now is None` will drop a still-present install.

chunk_findings.detail: The regular-file check and the read are not the same open, and `IsADirectoryError` was dropped from the handler. Interleaving: `p` is a regular file when `os.stat` runs, then it is replaced by a FIFO before `Path.read_bytes`; `read_bytes` opens the FIFO and blocks forever, which is the failure this change claims to avoid. If the replacement is a directory instead, `read_bytes` raises `IsADirectoryError`, which is no longer caught, so the call raises rather than returning None (the previous result, and still the result when the directory is visible at stat time).

A log of only `session.started` (matching harness), `session.prompt`, `task.added`, `lease.acquired` by the fake agent, `item.completed`, and `lease.released`, plus the new `git commit` of `.ddflow/events`, makes every `CORE` flag true. chunk_findings.detail: The new guide text says the smoke never installs a CLI and that a consented scratch-dir install is “a later step.” [D-agent-compat] (and the governing install-or-detect note) requires a missing CLI to be `unavailable` only when the operator did not consent, and with consent an install into a scratch dir only. This delta does not add consent or a scratch install in `detect`/`smoke`, so an operator who consented still gets `unavailable` and no install, and the docs now record that as intended.
